name: Archdiocese of Chicago

base: Every neighborhood was once a parish and every parish was once a nation: Polish, Irish, Lithuanian, Italian, Mexican. The churches are enormous and the people who built them are buried behind them.
The archdiocese has been consolidating for a generation and calls it renewal. Pastors run two or three churches and drive between them on Sunday mornings.
The presbyterate is proud of a tradition of pastoral independence that the chancery finds inconvenient.

byNeed.critically_short: A man is given a cluster of three parishes at five years ordained because there is no one else.
byNeed.stretched: Retirements outrun ordinations every year, and the personnel board has stopped pretending otherwise.
byNeed.adequate: The seminary and a steady flow of Polish and Mexican priests keep the numbers respectable.
byNeed.deep_bench: A rare year: more priests than the consolidated parishes need, and the young ones wait.

byFinancial.healthy: The sale of closed churches has, for the moment, balanced the books.
byFinancial.strained: The schools are the wound: every year the archdiocese closes a few more and every closing is a fight.
byFinancial.crisis: Parishes are being merged by the dozen, and the reason given is the money because the truth is worse.

byTension.one_voice: A quiet presbyterate, disciplined by decades of the same kind of archbishop.
byTension.quietly_split: The old ethnic pastors and the new men do not disagree in public. They simply do not attend the same things.
byTension.openly_divided: A priests' association meets without the archbishop's blessing and publishes letters he has to answer.

complications: A consolidation plan, already public, that will merge half the city's parishes into 'communities' with one pastor each.
Three parishes in serious financial trouble, with a fixer likely to be noticed.
A school system losing enrollment at a rate the archdiocese has stopped publishing.
A presbyterate at war with itself over the last archbishop's decisions.
hiddenComplications: The vicar for clergy keeps a private list of men he does not intend to make pastors, and the list is long.
An investigation into the finances of a closed parish that the chancery is trying to keep internal.
The archbishop's health is worse than the diocese knows.
